newsitem.title: UK: Pearson climbs as results top forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Pearson climbs as results top forecasts.

text.p: Shares in media and leisure group Pearson Plc opened higher on Monday after the group reported a surge in interim profits and said it aimed to double the value of the company within the next five years.
The shares were 11-1/2p higher at 677-1/2p by 0730 GMT.
Earlier, Pearson revealed that half-year pretax profits had soared to 81 million stg from 30 million stg in the same period last year.
Profits from continuing operations almost doubled to 65.5 million stg compared with a consensus forecast of 46 million stg.

"The results were ahead of our expectations and there was a very positive statement," said one media analyst who declined to be named. "But there's nothing about restructuring or selling off anything and that's why the share-price isn't too great."
Shares in Pearson have underperformed the FTSE 100 index by over nine percent since the beginning of June.
"The shares have had a terrible time over the last few weeks," the analyst said. "I expect they will now claw back some of those losses."
Analysts said the main features of Pearson's first half performance were the surge in profits at the Financial Times newspaper and the contribution from U.S. publisher Putnam Berkley.

Profits from the Financial Times increased to 22.4 million stg from 3.5 million whilst Putnam Berkley was "surpassing expectations". But disappointment came from the three Lazard houses where profits were significantly below 1996 levels.
Elsewhere, the company's statement was optimistic, analysts said, with promises of further growth in revenues and operating profits in the second half.
"They have also committed themselves to double-digit earnings growth...but they should be delivering that anyway," one analyst said.
